# Margince AI: test results

<!-- Generated from the invocation-site census, the scenario corpus and the committed records; do not edit by hand. -->

Which AI you can use, both ways, is on one page: [Which AI can I use with Margince?](which-ai-you-can-use.md). The results for an assistant a user connects are in [Your AI assistant: test results](mcp-tool-coverage.md).

Which features of Margince AI you can rely on under each model setup: which AI
model does which kind of work. Every grade here was measured by running the
product's real prompts against the model.

<details>
<summary>How this page is made</summary>

Generated by `cd backend && go test ./internal/compose/aicert/ -run TestAICertificationPage -update-ai-cert`; do not edit by hand. It reads the same
three trees `make e2e-ai-report` reads: the sites this build registers, the
scenarios under [`backend/internal/compose/aicert/corpus/`](../../backend/internal/compose/aicert/corpus/README.md),
and the records under [`backend/internal/compose/aicert/records/`](../../backend/internal/compose/aicert/records/README.md).

[`ai-certification.json`](ai-certification.json) beside this page holds the same
numbers, whole, for a reader who wants to ask a question this page does not
answer. This page is rendered from that file.

Nothing here is a merge gate. The certification lane is paid, manual and
BYOK-gated, so a prompt edit turns a record `stale` rather than failing a build.

How to add a case: [write-a-certification-case.md](../how-to/write-a-certification-case.md).
How to certify a model: [certify-an-ai-model.md](../how-to/certify-an-ai-model.md).

</details>

## Which model family should I use?

*"I want to run Margince on Gemini. Can I trust it?"* This is the answer for each
family of AI models, across everything Margince AI does. A *place* is one spot in the
product where a feature calls a model; one feature can call from several places. To start
from a ready-made setup instead, go to [Can I use this model setup?](#can-i-use-this-model-setup).

| Family | Models we tested | Can I trust it? | In plain words | Tries right | Quality scored by |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Claude | `claude-haiku-5-5`, `claude-sonnet-5-5` | 🟡 Mostly | Ready in 38 of the 55 places we tested; 1 more work if someone looks over the result; 16 more right every time, on too few tries to grade alone. | 1476 of 1494 | `gemini-3.1-flash-lite`, `gemini-3.8-flash` |
| Gemini | `gemini-3.1-flash-lite`, `gemini-3.8-flash` | 🟡 Mostly | Ready in 39 of the 55 places we tested; 4 more work if someone looks over the result; 12 more right every time, on too few tries to grade alone. | 1523 of 1530 | `claude-sonnet-5-5` |
| GPT | `gpt-6-luna`, `gpt-6-sol`, `gpt-oss-120b` | 🟡 Mostly | Ready in 22 of the 46 places we tested; 4 more work if someone looks over the result; 6 not reliable yet; 14 more right every time, on too few tries to grade alone. | 1067 of 1110 | `claude-sonnet-4-6`, `claude-sonnet-5-5` |
| Mistral | `ministral-14b-2512`, `ministral-8b-2512`, `mistral-medium-3-5` | 🔴 Not yet | Ready in 15 of the 41 places we tested; 6 more work if someone looks over the result; 9 not reliable yet; 11 more right every time, on too few tries to grade alone. | 648 of 708 | `claude-sonnet-4-6`, `claude-sonnet-5-5` |
| Gemma | `gemma-4-26b-a4b-it` | ⚪ Not enough tested yet | Tested in only 5 of the 64 places. Ask before relying on it. | 145 of 162 | `claude-sonnet-4-6` |

**The families above were scored by different judges.** A judge is the second model that scores how good an
answer is, and two judges do not score on one scale. Until one judge has scored them all, compare families on
*Tries right*: how often the answer passed its mechanical check, which no judge decides.

A family rated **Yes** is ready in every place we tested. One rated **Mostly** has at least 80 in every 100 tested places ready or working with a check, and one rated **Not yet** has fewer. We say **Not enough tested yet** when we tested it in under half of the places. A family is judged on its best model for each place, and only on the models a model setup uses, each in the places that setup sends to it.

## Can I use this model setup?

A model setup picks which AI model runs each feature, so the same feature can be
ready under one setup and not under another. Each one is a ready-made
[preset file](../../config/presets/README.md) an operator copies into the configuration.

117 of the 197 grades below were measured on an older version of the product and
are waiting to be re-checked; each is marked below.

| Model setup | Where your data goes | ✅ Ready | ⚠️ Usable with care | ❌ Not reliable yet | ❔ Not measured | Bottom line |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| [Google Gemini](#google-gemini) | global cloud | 27 | 10 | 0 | 1 | 27 of 38 features ready (10 re-checks pending) |
| [Google Gemini in the EU, through Vertex AI](#google-gemini-in-the-eu-through-vertex-ai) | EU-hosted cloud | 27 | 10 | 0 | 1 | 27 of 38 features ready (10 re-checks pending) |
| [Anthropic Claude](#anthropic-claude) | global cloud | 34 | 3 | 0 | 1 | 34 of 38 features ready (11 re-checks pending) |
| [OpenAI GPT-6, through OpenRouter](#openai-gpt-6-through-openrouter) | global cloud | 19 | 3 | 3 | 13 | 19 of 38 features ready (re-check pending) |
| [Open models from OpenAI and Mistral, through OpenRouter](#open-models-from-openai-and-mistral-through-openrouter) | global cloud | 12 | 12 | 7 | 7 | 12 of 38 features ready (re-check pending) |
| [Gemma 4 you could run yourself, through OpenRouter](#gemma-4-you-could-run-yourself-through-openrouter) | global cloud | 1 | 0 | 4 | 33 | 1 of 38 features ready (re-check pending) |
| [Mistral models in the EU, through OpenRouter](#mistral-models-in-the-eu-through-openrouter) | EU-hosted cloud | 11 | 2 | 12 | 13 | 11 of 38 features ready (re-check pending) |
| [Gemma 4 on your own server, through Ollama](#gemma-4-on-your-own-server-through-ollama) | your own servers | 0 | 0 | 0 | 38 | 0 of 38 features ready |
| [Qwen3 on your own server, through vLLM](#qwen3-on-your-own-server-through-vllm) | your own servers | 0 | 0 | 0 | 38 | 0 of 38 features ready |

**These grades were scored by 4 different judges** (`claude-sonnet-4-6`, `claude-sonnet-5-5`, `gemini-3.1-flash-lite`, `gemini-3.8-flash`). A judge is the second model that
scores how good an answer is, and two judges do not score on one scale: each feature below names its own.

**What the grades mean**

| Grade | What we measured | What to do |
|---|---|---|
| ✅ Ready | Right in at least 90 of every 100 of at least 12 tries, and so very likely right in at least 80 of every 100 calls; no test case clearly broken, and good answers. It holds for the test cases we ran, at the scope shown beside it. | Turn it on and rely on it. |
| ⚠️ Usable with care | Right in at least two thirds of tries, and acceptable answers. | Turn it on, and have someone look over what it produces. |
| ❌ Not reliable yet | Wrong too often, or answers below the quality bar. | Leave it off, or check every answer by hand. |
| ❔ Not measured | This model setup has a model for the feature, but nobody has tested it yet. | Ask for a test before relying on it. |

The small line under a grade names the model that answers the feature and its tier,
then the model a failed call falls back to and that model's own grade on the feature.
The router falls back only when a call fails: an error, a timeout, an answer broken
off midway. It never falls back because an answer was wrong, so a fallback does not
rescue a feature graded below. *no separate fallback* means both tiers bind the same model.

A count followed by *at least N%* gives the cautious end of the margin. With that many
tries, the feature is very likely right at least that often.
A grade marked *one model call of it* or *one turn of it* comes from a test that reaches only
that part of the feature. It says nothing about the rest.
The name after *scored by* is the model that judged the answers' quality. Grades from two
judges are not on one scale.

*re-check pending* after a grade means the product has changed since it was
measured. The grade is the last one we have, and it is shown until the next test replaces it.
[How the scoring works](#how-the-scoring-works) explains how a grade is reached.

## How the scoring works

1. **Real test cases.** Every feature has a set of test cases: a realistic
   situation (an email, an account, a web page) and the answer we expect. The
   model receives the same prompt the product sends in real use.
2. **Several tries.** Each test case is run 3 times at first (`RUNS=` can change
   that for one run), because a model can answer the same question differently
   each time. A test case whose result sits close to a line gets 3 more tries at a
   time, up to 12, so a close call is settled by more evidence rather than by luck.
   A feature is never graded ✅ Ready on fewer than 12 tries in all: one that looks ready
   sooner gets more tries first.
3. **Two checks on every try.**
   - *Is it right?* The answer is checked mechanically against what we expect: the
     right label, the right record, no invented facts.
   - *Is it good?* A second AI model, chosen so that it is not the one being tested,
     scores the answer from 0 to 100 against a written description of a good answer.
     A test case whose own check already sees everything that description asks is
     *checked mechanically* instead: no scoring model is asked, and it counts on its
     right answers alone.
4. **A close score is checked again.** The scoring model grades every try once. A
   score within 10 points of one of the test case's bars is asked for a second time,
   and two readings more than 5 apart for a third; the middle one counts (the
   average, of two). So one odd reading cannot decide a close call, and a clear one
   is not paid for 3 times.
5. **The grade.** All the tries of a feature are then read together:

| Grade | Right answers | Every test case | Quality |
|---|---|---|---|
| ✅ Ready | at least 90 of every 100 of at least 12 tries, and enough tries to be sure of at least 80 | right in at least half its tries, and not clearly broken | good on average across all tries, even allowing for doubt, and scored on at least 3 tries of every test case |
| ⚠️ Usable with care | at least two thirds of all tries | not failing nearly every try, and not clearly very poor | acceptable on average, even allowing for doubt |
| ❌ Not reliable yet | anything less, or a test case the scoring model never scored | | |

A feature does not have to be perfect to be ready: a stray miss or a low score
among many tries is allowed, because the grade weighs all of them together. A
test case that is clearly broken (one that fails nearly every try, or scores
below its acceptable bar on every try) holds the whole feature back however
well the others do.

### Thresholds

| What | Threshold |
|---|---|
| Right answers needed for ✅ Ready | at least 90 of every 100 tries, counted over all of the feature's test cases |
| How sure that must be, for ✅ Ready | the pass rate's lower bound at least 80 of every 100 |
| Fewest tries for ✅ Ready | 12, counted over all of the feature's test cases |
| Fewest quality scores for ✅ Ready | 3 on every test case a judge scores |
| Each test case, for ✅ Ready | right in at least 50 of every 100 of its own tries |
| Right answers needed for ⚠️ Usable with care | at least two thirds of all tries |
| A test case is clearly broken | its pass rate's upper bound is under 50 of every 100 (blocks ✅ Ready and ⚠️ Usable with care), or its quality score's upper bound is under its acceptable bar (blocks ✅ Ready) |
| Tries per test case | 3 at first (`RUNS=` changes it for one run); a borderline case gets 3 more at a time, up to 12 |
| Quality opinions per try | 1; a 2nd when it is within 10 points of a bar or under the lowest, a 3rd when the two are more than 5 apart; the middle one counts |
| How sure every bound is | one-sided 90% (z = 1.2816 for a pass rate, Student's t for an average score, whose spread is taken as at least 5 points) |
| Quality bar 70 / 50 / 40: 171 test cases | ✅ Ready needs scores averaging at least 70, allowing for doubt, no case whose best-case average is under 70, and no single try under 40; ⚠️ Usable with care needs at least 50, and no case whose best-case average is under 40 |
| Quality bar 80 / 60 / 50: 39 test cases | ✅ Ready needs scores averaging at least 80, allowing for doubt, no case whose best-case average is under 80, and no single try under 50; ⚠️ Usable with care needs at least 60, and no case whose best-case average is under 50 |
| Quality bar 75 / 55 / 45: 2 test cases | ✅ Ready needs scores averaging at least 75, allowing for doubt, no case whose best-case average is under 75, and no single try under 45; ⚠️ Usable with care needs at least 55, and no case whose best-case average is under 45 |

All of these live in [`backend/internal/compose/aicert/thresholds.go`](../../backend/internal/compose/aicert/thresholds.go) (quality bars: in each test case's file); change them there and regenerate this page.

<details>
<summary>The exact rule</summary>

From `Verdict` in [`score.go`](../../backend/internal/compose/aicert/score.go), applied to every case of a task at once:

```text
certified          = N ≥ 12 ∧ K/N ≥ 90% ∧ WilsonLower(K, N) ≥ 80%
                   ∧ every case passes ≥ 50% of its own n runs
                   ∧ TLower(score − its case's certified_min, over every graded run) ≥ 0
                   ∧ every case's TUpper(scores) ≥ its certified_min
                   ∧ every judged case has ≥ 3 graded runs
                   ∧ every graded run's score ≥ its case's floor
                   ∧ no case vetoed
supported_degraded = K ≥ ⌈2N/3⌉
                   ∧ TLower(score − its case's degraded_min, over every graded run) ≥ 0
                   ∧ no case vetoed
otherwise          = not_supported, which includes any case no judge graded
a case declaring judge: none meets every judge condition by construction,
and its runs enter no margin; its pass count is pooled like any other
vetoed             = WilsonUpper(k, n) < 50% ∨ TUpper(its scores) < its floor ∨ leaked
leaked             = a privacy case with a run that broke a privacy check, or,
                     judged, a run not refused yet ungraded or scored at or under its floor
WilsonLower/Upper  = the one-sided 90% Wilson score bounds (z = 1.2816)
TLower/TUpper      = mean ∓ t(0.90, m−1)·max(sd, 5)/√m over m values; the mean itself when m = 1
```

Each case sets its own quality bands: `certified_min`, `degraded_min` and `floor`.
So the pooled judge criterion averages every run's distance from its own case's bar.
Every run is graded once, and again when that score is within 10 of any of its case's bands.
It is graded a third time when the two differ by more than 5, at most 3 opinions. It scores at the
median of the opinions that parsed (the mean of two).
A case runs 3 times, then 3 more at a time up to 12 while it is borderline: its pass
count k of n satisfies (2k − n)² ≤ n, or its median score is within one standard
error of `certified_min` or `degraded_min`. Every case extends while the pool is
undecided, in one of three ways. The pooled pass rate is at least 90% but its Wilson bound
is under 80%. The pooled `certified_min` margin averages at least 0 but its bound is under 0.
Or the pool holds fewer than 12 runs while its rate is at least 90%. The decision reads only
scored runs, so a resumed run replays the same extensions.
The grades map to the record's words as ✅ Ready = `certified`, ⚠️ Usable with care = `supported_degraded`, ❌ Not reliable yet = `not_supported`, and
❔ Not measured = no record for that model.

</details>

<summary>Totals, and why the records went stale</summary>

### Totals

| | |
|---|---:|
| Shipped invocation sites | 64 |
| … best state `current` | 50 |
| … best state `partial` | 0 |
| … best state `stale` | 12 |
| … `absent` on every binding | 2 |
| Scenarios in the corpus | 350 |
| Committed records | 463 |
| Bindings measured | 20 |

#### Why the stale records went stale

Counted per record (one task and binding pair) over the 374 stale record(s) this build can attribute. A record covers every site its task ships, so the JSON beside this page carries it once per site: its 597 `stale_cause` entries are these 374 records. A record appears on more than one row below when a change moved a case and the prompt built from it together.

| What moved | Records | What it means |
|---|---:|---|
| the case | 131 | The test case changed. Re-certify: the old result measured a different case. |
| **the prompt this build sends** | 289 | The product changed. The band measured the old prompt, so it says nothing about the new one. Re-certify: a drop then is the cost of that change and not the model. |
| how a run is graded | 372 | What the judge is asked, or the rule that turns its scores into a grade, changed. A band can shift with neither the test nor the product touched. |

A site's *best* state is the strongest state any of its bindings reached. A
site `current` on one model and `stale` on three is counted once, as
`current`; the per-binding truth is in the tables below.

</details>

<details>
<summary>How to read the tables below</summary>

### How to read this page

| Word | What it means |
|---|---|
| Task | One job the product does with a model, such as `draft_reply` or `cold_start`. |
| Site | One spot inside a task where the product asks a model something. A task can have several: `cold_start` asks four separate questions, so it has four sites. Everything on this page is counted per site, because that is what a test case names. |
| Scenario | One test case: what the model is given, and what a good answer looks like. |
| Binding | The exact setup a model was tested on: who supplies it, which model, and where it runs. A result counts for that setup only: the same model reached another way has to be tested again. |
| Record | The saved result of one paid test run: one binding, one task. |
| Band | The grade a record gives its setup. `certified`: good enough to ship. `supported_degraded`: it works, but worse. `not_supported`: do not ship it. On a site's own row, `too_few_runs`: every test case of the site was right on its own, on too few tries for the site to have a grade of its own; its task's grade counts them. |
| Judge | The model that scored how good the answers were. Scores from two judges are not on one scale, so compare two records' quality only when they name the same judge. |
#### The four states

A state says whether a saved result still describes the product as it is
today. It says nothing about how well the model did; that is the band.

| State | What it claims |
|---|---|
| `current` | Still true. Nothing it tested has changed, and there is no test case it missed. |
| `partial` | Still true about what it tested, but test cases have been added since that it never saw. The `Scenarios` column says how many of each. |
| `stale` | Out of date. Something it tested has changed since: a test case, or the wording the product now sends. The grade no longer describes what ships, and the run has to be paid for again. |
| `absent` | Never tested on any setup. Its columns are dashes because nothing has measured it. |

#### The numbers

| Column | What it says |
|---|---|
| Quality | Who scores how good a test case's answers are: `judge`, a second model, or `checked mechanically`, where the case's own check sees everything a judge would and no judge is asked. |
| Runs, Passed | How many times the model was asked, and how often it did what the test case wanted. |
| Reliability | Passed divided by Runs, then its Wilson interval in brackets, from the formula and z the verdict uses. A band reads the lower end of a site's pooled rate and the upper end of each case alone. A binding or family row is graded by no band. Treat a change as real only when the intervals do not overlap or the band changes. |
| `accepted`, `wrong_answer`, `invalid`, `abstained` | What kind of answer came back. This is a different split from pass/fail. Some test cases want the model to decline, and an answer it gave instead is a failure even though it counts as `accepted`. |
| Scenarios | How many of the site's test cases the saved result still covers, out of how many the site has today. |
| Record p50, p95 | How long answers took: the middle one, and a slow one (only 1 in 20 was slower). Both belong to the whole test run, not to the single site whose table they appear in, so a run covering several sites shows the same pair on each. |
| Slowest p95 | The worst p95 of any run in that row. It is never an average, because an average of these numbers is a figure nothing measured. |
| `-` | Not measured. No runs is not a reliability of zero, and no timing is not a fast one. Older results carry one stamp for the whole task instead of one per test case, so their `Scenarios` cell is a dash too. |

</details>

**Best model tested** is the strongest result that still describes what ships.
Only a `current` or `partial` record is eligible; among those the pick is the
best band, then the best reliability, then the fastest.

Read the band beside it before running anything on it. `certified` is a safe
pick. `supported_degraded` works, but worse. `not_supported` means the best
model anyone has measured on that site still is not good enough to ship, so it
names work to do. A dash means every result for that
site is out of date or missing, and the State column says which.

<details>
<summary>Stale records, and why</summary>

### Stale records, and why

A record goes stale when a scenario it measured changes, when the prompt
this build now builds from that scenario changes, or when how a run is graded
changes. The stamp covers all three, so a prompt edit invalidates a record that
never mentioned it. A scenario the
record never saw does not make it stale; that is `partial`.

*Predates per-scenario stamps* means the record carries one stamp for the
whole task and nothing finer, so it can only say that something it measured
moved, and never which case. Re-certifying it costs the whole task; a record
with per-scenario stamps names the cases, and costs only those.

Re-certify with `make e2e-ai TASK=<task> MODEL=<provider:model>` (paid: real
model, real network).

<details>
<summary>Decision models</summary>

### Decision models

A decision model answers a site's closed question first. The site's LLM ladder
answers instead whenever the lane is unbound, fails,
or answers below the site's own floor. A decision record comes from a
`make e2e-ai ROUTING=` run whose config binds `decisions:`, and is certified
per site with no judge: `certified` means no answer the site kept was wrong in
any run, and at least one was kept. A bound lane answers every site whether or
not a record exists (advisory, not a runtime gate). *Certified row* here means
the record is certified on at least 15 kept answers and not stale. An operator
trusts the binding on such a row. `make gen` writes those rows into
`internal/modules/ai/decisioncert_gen.go`.

| Site | Binding | State | Verdict | Certified row | Runs | Kept | Kept wrong | Fallback rate | Fallbacks by reason | Served pass rate |
|---|---|---|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|---:|
| `capture_confidentiality_verdict/thread` | `gemini_decision · gemini-decision-1 · cloud_frontier` | `current` | `certified` | yes | 288 | 243 | 0 | 0.16 | `below_floor` 45 | 1.00 |
| `capture_counterparty_verdict/verdict` | `gemini_decision · gemini-decision-1 · cloud_frontier` | `stale`: 19 scenarios it scored have changed since (the prompt this build sends): a_chased_cold_pitch_is_still_a_vendor_pitch, a_company_writing_as_itself_does_not_become_a_contact_named_after_it, a_department_display_name_is_not_somebodys_name, a_fluent_machine_written_pitch_is_still_a_vendor_pitch, a_private_property_desk_the_owner_wrote_to_is_not_a_contact, a_trade_offices_city_mailbox_names_a_place_not_a_contact and 13 more (it also scored a_numbered_support_queue_is_one_desk, a_shared_mailbox_is_real_correspondence_with_nobody_to_name, which the corpus no longer holds) | `certified` | no | 147 | 144 | 0 | 0.02 | `below_floor` 3 | 1.00 |
| `site_triage/triage` | `gemini_decision · gemini-decision-1 · cloud_frontier` | `current` | `certified` | yes | 15 | 15 | 0 | 0.00 | - | 1.00 |
| `site_triage/triage` | `jev_compatible · typesafe/jev-1.13 · cloud_frontier` | `current` | `certified` | yes | 15 | 15 | 0 | 0.00 | - | 1.00 |

says what a site is scored against; the record table says how each binding
did. What the columns mean is in [How to read this page](#how-to-read-this-page).
